newsitem.title: UK: HRT does not protect heart short-term, study finds.
newsitem.headline: HRT does not protect heart short-term, study finds.

text.p: Finnish and British researchers said on Friday they feared hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may not prevent heart disease in women, at least not in the short-term.
They said a review of 22 separate trials showed no significant difference in heart disease rates between women who got the hormones and women who did not.

Klim McPherson of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and Elina Hemminkiof the Health Services Research Unit in Helsinki said long-term trials, which are underway, could show different outcomes.
"The results of these pooled data do not support the notion that postmenopausal hormone therapy prevents cardiovascular events," they wrote in a report in the British Medical Journal.
"It is quite possible that long term effects are different, both for cardiovascular diseases and for cancer," they added.

Doctors widely believe that HRT, which replaces female hormones lost during the menopause, can help stop women from developing "male" patterns of disease. This would include a greater tendency to heart disease.
There is clear evidence HRT helps prevent osteoporosis. But it may increase the risk of endometrial cancer.
